original_question: In the same setting of a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with an invariant interior component U and limiting map g: U -> C^2, suppose g has a fixed point in U and rank one, so that g is a retraction onto a Siegel disk. Can g instead be a retraction onto a Herman ring, or onto a punctured Siegel disk?
target_in_paper: §4, "Stable regions for complex Hénon type maps" (Milnor), Question 1, Rank One Case (p. 9): "Can g be a retraction onto a Herman ring (or onto a punctured Siegel disk)?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the exact target. It correctly identifies the ambient setting of a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2, an interior component U, a subsequential limit map g, the rank-one case, the fixed-point discussion, the Siegel-disk retraction, and the two precise alternative targets named in the paper: a Herman ring and a punctured Siegel disk.
missing_details: The paper defines the ambient dynamical set as K^+(f), the set of points in C^2 with bounded forward orbit, and U is a connected component of int K^+(f), with int K^+(f) assumed nonempty.
The map g is not an arbitrary map U -> C^2; it is the limit of a convergent subsequence of the iterates of f restricted to U, obtained via Montel's theorem.
The section first asks whether U can be wandering; the rank-one subquestion belongs to the complementary nonwandering/periodic setting.
In the nonwandering case, the paper explicitly replaces f by a finite iterate so that f(U)=U; this reduction is part of the local setup for the rank-one question.
The paper also records that in this periodic setting f commutes with g; this is part of the nearby context that your draft leaves implicit.
The Jacobian determinant δ of f should be named, since the paper notes that rank(g) is 0 or 1 only when |δ|<1, while rank 2 occurs when |δ|=1.

As written, your draft slightly compresses the logic of the paper by simultaneously assuming the paper's Siegel-disk conclusion and then asking about the excluded alternatives. The paper's nearby wording is: if g has a fixed point in U, then one gets a Siegel-disk retraction; the open question is whether a rank-one limit map can instead retract onto a Herman ring or punctured Siegel disk.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the symbols f, K^+(f), U, g, and δ should all be defined explicitly.
refined_question: Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with Jacobian determinant δ, and suppose that K^+(f) := {z in C^2 : the forward orbit {f^n(z)} is bounded} has nonempty interior. Let U be a connected component of int K^+(f) that is not wandering; after replacing f by a finite iterate, assume f(U)=U. Let g: U -> C^2 be the limit of a convergent subsequence of the iterates f^n|_U. In the rank-one case (so rank(g)=1, hence |δ|<1 in the paper's setup), Milnor notes that if g has a fixed point in U, then g is a retraction of U onto a Siegel disk. Can such a rank-one limit map g instead be a retraction of U onto a Herman ring, or onto a punctured Siegel disk?
justification: The draft is targeting the narrow subquestion in §4, Question 1, Rank One Case, rather than the broader wandering-component question or the neighboring rank-zero and rank-two cases. The surrounding lines on p. 9 supply the hidden assumptions: the definition of K^+(f), the choice of U as a connected component of int K^+(f), the subsequential-limit definition of g, the reduction to the periodic case f(U)=U after replacing f by an iterate, the commutation of f and g, and the rank/Jacobian dichotomy. I therefore kept the question tightly centered on Milnor's exact rank-one problem and did not broaden it. This paper is a problem list, so there is no relevant Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 here; the exact target is the explicitly stated Rank One Case in §4.
